title: Space-time duality approach to (inhomogeneous) integrable quenches
authors: Riccardo Travaglino, Pasquale Calabrese, Katja Klobas, Bruno Bertini
abstract: Characterising the universal aspects of non-equilibrium quantum many-body dynamics is one of the key goals of this century's physics research. Progress, however, is hindered by the lack of general theoretical frameworks for studying interacting quantum matter far from equilibrium. A recent breakthrough has been the realization that several key non-equilibrium quantities, such as the rate of growth of entanglement or the fluctuations of conserved charges within finite subsystems, can be related to equilibrium properties through a space-time duality that effectively exchanges the roles of space and time. This observation effectively enables the study of non-equilibrium phenomena using tools and concepts borrowed from equilibrium statistical mechanics and thermodynamics. A first proof of principle of this framework, dubbed space-time duality approach (SDA), was provided by interacting integrable systems, where thermodynamic properties can often be characterized exactly, while dynamical quantities typically remain beyond analytical reach. Subsequent developments, however, revealed that the SDA suffered from an intrinsic ambiguity, restricting its applicability to homogeneous quenches and to charge fluctuations arising from symmetric initial states. Here we resolve this ambiguity from first principles and derive closed-form predictions for entanglement growth and charge fluctuations after general quantum quenches. We benchmark our results against the exact analytical solution of the Rule 54 quantum cellular automaton and extensive TEBD simulations of the XXZ chain. Moreover we show that, when specialised to the entanglement entropy, our framework naturally reproduces the predictions of the quasiparticle picture.
summary: The paper develops and refines a Space-Time Duality Approach (SDA) to analyze non-equilibrium dynamics in integrable quantum many-body systems. It resolves previous theoretical ambiguities to provide exact analytical formulas for quantities like entanglement growth and charge fluctuations following general quenches. This advances the understanding of how equilibrium concepts can be used to solve complex, out-of-equilibrium physics problems.
main_problem: Characterizing universal aspects of non-equilibrium quantum many-body dynamics, particularly for interacting systems far from equilibrium.
main_result: The authors derive closed-form analytical predictions for entanglement growth and charge fluctuations after general inhomogeneous quenches in integrable systems by resolving ambiguities in the space-time duality approach (SDA).
method: They employ the Space-Time Duality Approach (SDA), which maps non-equilibrium dynamics to stationary properties of a dual theory, utilizing generalized Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz (TBA) equations and Generalized Hydrodynamics (GHD).
model_or_system: The study focuses on one-dimensional integrable quantum systems, exemplified by the XXZ spin chain model. The analysis covers both gapped ($\Delta > 1$) and gapless ($\Delta \le 1$) regimes.
key_observables: Entanglement growth (Rényi entropies $S_\alpha$), fluctuations of conserved charges, and one-point functions of local operators.
important_parameters: The quench protocol is general and inhomogeneous; key limits include the homogeneous quench limit ($\zeta=0$) and the Von Neumann limit ($\alpha 	o 1$).
main_assumptions: The initial state $|\psi_0angle$ is assumed to have short-range correlations, and the framework relies on assuming scale invariance for bipartite quenches.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate tensor-network diagrams showing local expectation values under circuit evolution and map out the duality between entropy calculations in the original and dual channels. Other figures show instantaneous slopes of Rényi entropies and FCS vs. time for the XXZ chain quench.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the SDA framework, resolves its intrinsic ambiguities by matching predictions to known results (like Rule 54), derives closed-form expressions using generalized TBA/GHD techniques, and benchmarks these analytical results against TEBD simulations of the XXZ chain.
why_interesting: This work provides powerful, general theoretical tools for understanding how quantum information spreads and thermalizes in interacting systems far from equilibrium, which is central to modern AMO physics research on open quantum systems.

Equivalently the tensor network can be contracted in space by replacing the space-transfer matrix T with the projector to its leading eigenvectors. (b): Duality from the original entropy of A at time t (dashed blue line) to the entropy in the dual channel at the boundary of A (full blue line). The light cone represents the region in which the occupation functions are a mixture of those of left and right states....
